title: Five Popular Sweets Around the World
summary: Meet gelato, baklava, mochi, churros, and alfajores. Compare their ingredients, forms, cooking methods, and textures.

cover.alt: Three adults at a sunlit cafe table share gelato, baklava, churros, and sandwich cookies.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Meet gelato, baklava, mochi, churros, and alfajores. Compare their ingredients, forms, cooking methods, and textures.

items.prompt: What do you think makes a sweet special?
What would you choose: a frozen sweet or a warm sweet?
What do you think is more important in a sweet: taste or texture?

blocks.title: Part 1: A Simple Way to Compare Sweets
paragraphs: We can ask four questions about a sweet. What ingredients are in it? What form does it have? How do people make it? What is its texture, or how does it feel in your mouth?

Gelato is a popular frozen sweet from Italy. Its main ingredients are milk, sugar, and flavour. Gelato has less air than ice cream, so it is denser. Dense food is closely packed, not light and full of air.

images.alt: On one side an adult serves a metal cup of gelato; on the other an adult cuts a tray of layered baklava.

blocks.title: Check: Part 1: A Simple Way to Compare Sweets

items.prompt: Why is gelato usually denser than ice cream?
items.answer: Gelato is usually denser because it has less air than ice cream.

blocks.title: Part 2: Baklava Has Many Layers
paragraphs: Baklava is a popular pastry sweet in Turkey and nearby countries. It has many thin layers of pastry with chopped nuts between them. Honey or sweet syrup goes over the pastry and soaks into it. “Soaks into” means the liquid enters the food.
Baklava and gelato have very different forms. Gelato is one frozen mixture. Baklava is built from many pastry layers, nuts, and sweet liquid.

blocks.title: Check: Part 2: Baklava Has Many Layers

items.prompt: What is between the thin pastry layers in baklava?
items.answer: Chopped nuts are between the thin pastry layers.

blocks.title: Part 3: Mochi Is Soft and Chewy
paragraphs: Mochi is a popular rice cake from Japan. It is made from sticky rice. People pound the rice, or hit it again and again, until it becomes soft and stretchy. Mochi has a chewy texture, so you must move your teeth many times when you eat it.
Some mochi has sweet bean paste inside. People can also eat it with other sweet toppings. Unlike layered baklava, mochi is a soft rice cake.

images.alt: On one side an adult pounds soft white mochi; on the other an adult fries golden churros and rolls them in sugar.

blocks.title: Check: Part 3: Mochi Is Soft and Chewy

items.prompt: How does sticky rice change when people make mochi?
items.answer: The rice becomes soft and stretchy when people pound it.

blocks.title: Part 4: Churros Are Fried
paragraphs: A churro is a popular fried dough sweet from Spain. Frying means cooking food in hot oil. The dough cooks until it is golden. People often roll the churro in sugar after frying it.
Churros are also eaten in Latin America. Some people eat them with thick hot chocolate. Their cooking method is different from gelato: churros go into hot oil, but gelato is frozen.

items.prompt: What often happens to a churro after it is fried?
items.answer: People often roll the fried churro in sugar.

blocks.title: Part 5: Alfajores Are Sandwich Cookies
paragraphs: An alfajor is a popular sweet in Argentina and other parts of South America. It is a sandwich cookie. Here, “sandwich” means that two round cookies hold a filling in the middle.

The filling is a sweet milk caramel. Some alfajores also have chocolate or sugar on the outside. Their form is different from baklava: an alfajor has two cookies around one centre, while baklava has many thin pastry layers.

blocks.title: Check: Part 5: Alfajores Are Sandwich Cookies

items.prompt: What is in the middle of an alfajor?
items.answer: A sweet milk caramel filling is in the middle of an alfajor.

blocks.title: Part 6: Five Sweets, Five Clear Differences
paragraphs: Now use the four questions. Gelato is a dense, frozen milk sweet. Baklava is layered pastry with nuts and syrup. Mochi is a chewy rice cake. A churro is fried dough, often with sugar. An alfajor is a sandwich cookie with milk caramel.
Their ingredients, forms, cooking methods, and textures make them different. One is frozen, one has many layers, one is chewy, one is fried, and one has two cookies around a filling.

images.alt: Two adults at a kitchen table make sandwich cookies with a thick milk caramel filling.

blocks.title: Check: Part 6: Five Sweets, Five Clear Differences

items.prompt: Which sweet is made from sticky rice?
items.answer: Mochi is made from sticky rice.
